alt: A block of a blockchain points to a Non-fungible token box that holds an author address, a smart contract address and a numeric ID. A getURLfromID call leads to a web link, which leads to the art, assets or files. Side notes say the token is owned and sellable, the file cannot be copyrighted just by this but can be owned, and what the link gives depends on the contract.
author: Alhadis

alt: The Ethereum logo with the label ERC-20 beside a grid of token logos and ticker symbols such as BNT, MANA, MATIC, WBTC and sUSD, all tokens built on the ERC-20 standard.
author: zephyrnet

alt: Five stacked layers. From the bottom: settlement layer (the Ethereum blockchain), asset layer (native asset ETH and tokens ERC-20 and ERC-721), protocol layer (exchange, lending, derivatives, asset management), application layer, and an aggregation layer with aggregators on top.
author: Fabian Schär

alt: Party 1 and Party 2 both agree to a smart contract at the top. The contract creates transactions, and the transactions are included in a block of a blockchain shown as a row of linked cubes.
author: Yujian Zhang

alt: A market map in seven columns: Experience, Discovery, Creator Economy, Spatial Computing, Decentralization, Human Interface and Infrastructure. Each column lists company logos, for example game makers under Experience, Ethereum and other blockchain projects under Decentralization, and cloud and network firms under Infrastructure.
author: Jon Radoff

alt: A paper wallet printout. On the left a Bitcoin address as text and a QR code marked SHARE. On the right the matching private key as text and a QR code marked SECRET.
author: LoganDeveloper

alt: A hand holds a hardware wallet. Its small screen shows a Send request with the total amount in BTC, the transaction fee, and the prompt Hold to sign, so the key signs on the device itself.
author: FlippyFlink

alt: Four transactions TX 1 to TX 4. Outputs of earlier transactions, each locked by a script, become the inputs of later ones. Outputs not yet used as an input are marked green as unspent, meaning available funds.
author: Wargo

alt: Two transactions. Left: one input of 50 BTC gives two outputs, 0.5 BTC to the receiver and 49.5 BTC back as change. Right: three inputs of 0.5, 0.1 and 0.2 BTC are merged into one output of 0.8 BTC.
author: Matthäus Wander

alt: A payer in JPY pays a payee in USD through a chain: JPY gateway, a JPY to CNY market maker, CNY to EUR, then EUR to USD, ending at the USD gateway. Green dashed arrows show the payment hopping along this path.
author: GiantGox

alt: A Ripple admin console on the Trust Lines tab. It lists trust lines for Japanese Yen, Bitcoin and ETH, each with a counterparty, balance, limit and settings such as rippling, frozen and auth.
author: GiantGox

alt: Order books for XRP/USD and XRP/EUR are combined into a bridged USD/EUR order book. That is merged with the direct USD/EUR order book to form one synthetic order book that mixes both.
author: GiantGox

alt: A five-step food supply chain: primary production, processing, distribution, retail and consumers. Each step lists the technology used. Distribution lists tracking and traceability, robotics and automation, and IoT blockchain.
author: Abdo Hassoun, Fatma Boukid, Antonella Pasqualone, Christopher J. Bryant, Guillermo García García, Carlos Parra-López, Sandeep Jagtap, Hana Trollman, Janna Cropotova, Francisco J. Barba
